To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have created a linelist of atomic lines which can be used for the description of infrared spectra of late M, L and T type ultracool dwarves, from 10 00 to 25 00 A, and that we have created plots showing how well our synthetic spectra match the observed Arcturus spectra and Sunspot umbr spectra in this wavelength range.

the atomic lines which are likely to be observable at high resolution in infrared spectra of ultracool dwarves are: Fe I, Fe II, Cr I, Cr II, Ti I, Ti II, Ca I, Ca II, Ni I, Ni II, Na I, Mg II, Si I, Si II, Al I, Al II, C I, C II, O I, O II, S I, S II, P I, P II, and H I.
we have identified 25 new infrared atomic lines which can be used in the modelling of the atmospheres of ultracool dwarars.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) the atomic linelist for ultracool dwarf stars; (2) the comparison of synthetic and observed spectra for the atomic lines in the infrared; (3) the comparison of atomic line strengths for Arcturus and the Sunspot umbra

the following: (i) the development of a new atomic linelist for the infrared spectral region, (ii) the comparison of the new atomic linelist with existing atomic linelists, (iii) the comparison of synthetic infrared spectra with observed spectra of Sunspot umbra and Arcturus, (iv) the development of an atomic line identification program, (v) the application of the atomic line identification program to infrared spectra of ultracool dwarars.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the atomic linelist is complete to a depth of 1.5-2.5 dex in the Sunspot umbral atmosphere.

the linelist is complete to 10 000 A and that the linelist has a few gaps from 10 500 A to 12 500 A and a few more gaps from 15 000 A to 18 000 A, with the largest gap being from 16 000 A to just over 17 000 A.
the synthetic spectra of Arcturs and Sunspot umbras reproduce the observed spectra well.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the infrared spectra of ultracool dwarves can be described with an atomic linelist of 10 elements, namely C, O, Mg, Si, Fe, Ca, Na, Ti, Cr and Mn, and a few molecular features, namely H _{2} O, CH, CN, TiO and VO.
we provide a set of 120 atomic lines which are likely to be observed in the infrared spectra of ultracool dwarves.
we present a linelist of 130 atomic lines for the spectral range 10 000-25 000 A and we provide the atomic parameters for these lines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the infrared spectra of ultracool dwarves can be modeled with atomic lines from a few dozen elements.
the majority of infrared atomic lines are very weak and therefore not useful in high resolution infrared spectroscopy.
there is a significant amount of infrared atomic line opacity in ultracool dwarf atmospheres, which is likely important for the determination of the effective temperature of ultracool dwarves.
